html:
Vere Cornwall Bird was the union leader who led Antigua and Barbuda for most of the second half of the 20th century, and its first prime minister at independence in 1981.

He rose through the Antigua Trades and Labour Union, founded after the labour unrest that swept the British Caribbean in the late 1930s, among the grandchildren of those freed in 1834. From the 1950s he headed the island's government, with a break in the 1970s, and led it to independence on 1 November 1981.

His Antigua Labour Party ran the country for decades, and his son Lester followed him as prime minister. Scandals over arms and money stained his later years. Antiguans still call him the father of the nation, alongside Viv Richards the best known Antiguan in the Commonwealth.
